name: Crucible Industries Tempest-12 'Widowmaker'
description:
The Crucible Industries Tempest-12 is a semi-automatic shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with an eight-round tube magazine, an extended barrel with interchangeable choke tubes, and a modular stock system that converts between a full rifle stock, a folding stock, and a pistol grip configuration. The Widowmaker is Crucible's general-purpose combat shotgun — less specialized than the Storm-12's breaching focus or the Maelstrom's area denial role.

The Tempest's interchangeable choke system allows the operator to adjust the weapon's spread pattern to match engagement conditions — cylinder bore for room clearing, modified for intermediate range, and full choke for slug work at extended distance. Combined with the modular stock, a single Tempest-12 can be configured for any shotgun role short of full-automatic fire. Field-swapping a choke tube takes fifteen seconds; stock conversion takes about the same.

Crucible positions the Tempest-12 as the shotgun for operators who don't know what they'll face until they're facing it. The weapon's adaptability has made it popular among independent contractors, bounty hunters, and security teams who operate across varied environments without the luxury of mission-specific weapon selection. The Widowmaker adapts because its users must.
legality: Legal — enhanced registration required; folding stock may require separate permit
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 30-50 meters (choke dependent)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 8+1 rounds
weight: 3.5 kg (full stock configuration)
tactical_use: A modular combat shotgun adaptable to varied engagement conditions. The interchangeable choke system provides pattern customization for different ranges. The modular stock system allows the weapon to be configured for the operational environment. The eight-round magazine provides adequate sustained fire capability. Suitable as a primary weapon for operators who face unpredictable threats across varied environments.
cultural_context: The Widowmaker is the independent operator's shotgun. Where corponation teams carry mission-specific weapons, independents carry a Tempest and adapt on the fly. The weapon has become associated with the self-reliant professional who works alone and needs every tool in one package. Its nickname is earned through use rather than marketing — the Tempest makes widows of the people who underestimate the operator carrying it.
story_hooks: A Widowmaker configured as a precision slug gun is used to make a shot at 75 meters that shouldn't be possible with a smoothbore shotgun — the operator is using saboted ammunition that nobody has seen before.

An independent operator's Tempest has been modified with a choke tube that contains a hidden compartment for smuggling small items through checkpoints. The modification is discovered when the choke fails catastrophically during a firefight.

physical_description.visual_profile: A purposeful, utilitarian combat shotgun with a distinctly modular architecture. The Tempest-12 presents as a sleek, purpose-built platform rather than a traditional hunting gun—its lines are clean and industrial, with visible quick-swap mechanical interfaces along the barrel and stock junction. The extended tube magazine extends noticeably beneath the forearm, creating a balanced mass distribution that suggests serious fieldwork capacity.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94-108 cm (stock dependent). Barrel length: 51 cm with interchangeable choke housing. Tube magazine: 25 cm. Width at receiver: 7.2 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but balanced—3.5 kg feels purposefully distributed rather than front-heavy, despite the extended magazine. Hefty enough to absorb recoil, light enough for sustained tactical movement. The weight settles comfortably in the hand rather than pulling downward.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel receiver and barrel. Polymer furniture (stock, grip panels, handguard). Aluminum alloy choke housing with stainless steel quick-change threads. Magazine tube: chrome-lined steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte black receiver with brushed steel barrel. The choke housing has a subtle satin finish with precision-cut threading marks visible near the muzzle. Polymer components show a textured, non-reflective matte black. Wear patterns visible on control surfaces—thumb safety, charging handle, magazine tube release.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte black receiver and polymer. Accent: brushed steel barrel, polished aluminum choke collar, Crucible Industries red accent stripe along the tube magazine (thin, corporate branding).
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with aggressive checkering on both the pistol grip and handguard. The safety lever and charging handle feature textured polymer overlays. Stock furniture (when attached) uses contoured grip panels with reinforced finger grooves.
distinctive_features: Hexagonal quick-change choke housing at muzzle—three different choke tubes visible in typical field kit
Modular stock receiver with color-coded quick-release lugs (red indicators for locked position)
Oversized charging handle with integrated cocking indicator
Extended tube magazine with witness holes showing round count at 2-round intervals
Picatinny rail section above receiver for mounting optics or iron sights
Aggressive venting ports along handguard to manage heat signature
Mechanical safety lever with tactile detents (safe/fire positions clearly defined)
Serial plate on left side of receiver with Crucible logo stamped in relief
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES logo stamped on the receiver side plate in bold sans-serif. 'TEMPEST-12' marked in smaller font below the logo. Serial number and manufacturing date code (GLMZ facility stamp) etched on the barrel. Choke tube housings individually marked (CYL, MOD, FULL) with laser-cut indicators.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field weapons show minor scuffing on receiver edges and handguard. Stock conversion hinges may show wear polish from repeated swaps. Barrel exhibits light carbon residue near the muzzle (post-fire appearance). Magazines typically show minor pressure marks from repeated loading. Well-maintained examples appear combat-ready but clearly used.
